question.problem:
Given that the function
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193886/assets/47e2bbdd0741bbac490c3ac0851e95b2103078e22d06d4a369712236529e8302.svg) 
is continuous at $x=1$, find the value of $a.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=1,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}{log}_{2}⁡(ax+1) \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(a(1)+1) \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(a+1),\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}({log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)) \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(2(1)+1) \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(3) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}g(x) \\ {log}_{2}⁡(a+1) & =1 \\ a+1 & ={2}^{1} \\ a & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
